text:
Oliver (Sales): Hey team — heads up, ACME Corp is asking for a one-time promotional discount to win the PO. Requesting 25% off list for year-1 (applied to subscription charges only), 12-month commit, $180k ARR. Also want a data-residency addendum (EU-only) and a slight tweak to liability cap. Have contract draft in DocuSign. Need deal desk approval to proceed.

Maria (Finance): @Oliver (Sales) thx. Can you confirm: ARR = $180k ARR is annual run rate at list price? Will they prepay or monthly billing? What’s the expected gross margin delta at 25%? Also flagging that discounts >20% need CFO signoff per policy.

Oliver (Sales): Confirm ARR is $180,000 at list before discount. They prefer monthly billing but have said they can do quarterly prepay if needed. At 25% straight discount the unit economics reduce expected gross margin by ~7 points (GPU op + infra). Customer is strategic — references + channel potential. Competitive pressure: two other vendors gave lower price.

DealDeskBot: Checklist: [x] ARR provided [x] Commit length provided [ ] Legal addendum needed [ ] CFO approval if >20% discount [x] Sales commission impact noted. Please attach final SOW and redlines.

Sam (Accounting): For invoicing: if they stay monthly we’ll need to apply a recurring discount code on subscription lines. If they prepay we’ll invoice one upfront line and apply a manual credit memo for the promotional portion. Revenue recognition note: if prepaid, we need to defer revenue over 12 months — confirm invoice method. Also request a GL tag: DEAL_ACME_2026.

Jenny (Legal): I pulled the draft. The requested change to liability cap increases risk; current standard cap is 1x fees, they want 3x for data-residency exposure. We should avoid expanding unlimited liability; propose adding carveout language for data processing obligations and keep cap at 1x with indemnity for data breaches limited to actual damages. Also need to review EU data addendum for routing.

Maria (Finance): Given the margin hit and policy: we can approve up to 20% at ops level but >20% requires Priya (CFO). Suggest counter-proposal: offer 20% discount + 30-day free onboarding credit and keep standard legal caps. That preserves unit economics and gives perceived value. Thoughts? :thinking_face:

Oliver (Sales): Counterproposal might lose them — competitor already offered 25%. Customer has a hard procurement deadline end of week. If we don’t land, they’ll go elsewhere. Can we escalate to CFO for a one-time exception of 25% but require sales to waive referral commission and accept 50% split on variable comp?

Priya (CFO): I reviewed the numbers and the strategic rationale. I can approve a one-time concession at 22% (applied to subscription lines for year 1 only). Conditions: 1) Legal to sign off on the data addendum without increasing cap beyond 1x fees; 2) Billing mode preferentially quarterly prepay and if they insist monthly we accept but revenue deferral rules apply; 3) Finance to create GL tag DEAL_ACME_2026 and record discount under promo bucket; 4) Sales compensation to be adjusted per @Sales Ops (suggest 50% split on accelerators for this deal). Oliver — proceed to get DocuSign updated and tag the contract with DEAL-ACME-2026. :white_check_mark:

Jenny (Legal): Acknowledged. I will push back on the 3x cap and ask for the 1x + specific indemnity language for data. Will update redline and seat with the customer today.

Sam (Accounting): Noted. I’ll prepare the invoice template for quarterly prepay and the manual credit flow if they choose monthly. Will add GL tag after contract is final.

Oliver (Sales): Thanks everyone — I’ll update the deal in Salesforce, apply the discount code, and route the final contract to DocuSign. Targeting signature EOD Fri. Appreciate the quick turnaround. :pray:
